candidates.corridor: Upper Gila Wilderness / Grapevine to Mogollon Creek
candidates.routeEvidence: American Whitewater documents a 42-mile Class III expedition, a direct USGS Gila-near-Gila gauge, a 200 cfs minimum and 1,200 cfs upper reference; Dreamflows repeats those same-reach triggers.
candidates.accessAndRisk: American Whitewater says the only emergency exit is a trail at Sapillo Creek leading many miles to Highway 15. The published start depends on Grapevine Campground or a highway bridge, and the takeout is described as a campground past Mogollon Creek. A current authoritative reopening and public boating access record for Grapevine was not located; recent route reporting documents numerous changing strainers and elevated danger after the 2022 flood.
candidates.decision: Do not publish until a local expert confirms current public water-entry and take-out rights, campground/road status, current strainer hazards and an appropriate audience warning. Strong numeric flow support alone does not clear the remote-rescue and access gate.

candidates.routeEvidence: American Whitewater's Feb. 2026 route update describes a 13-mile Class II-IV run on direct USGS 08378500 with a 170-250 cfs boatable-flow range and named public access areas.
candidates.accessAndRisk: The guide recommends going with a small experienced local A-Team, warns that eddies and stops are limited, line choices are narrow, and wood/snags change. The 2023 State Parks draft plan and current land-access history document fences, shallow rocky water and public-access conflicts; Mora Campground is currently closed for construction through 2027, removing one named access in the chain.
candidates.decision: Keep held pending current access-by-access confirmation and local expert hazard review. The new flow guidance improves score support but does not yet clear the safety/access publication gate for any specific endpoint pair.

candidates.corridor: Cimarron River / Eagle Nest to Cimarron
candidates.routeEvidence: American Whitewater lists a 23.6-mile Class III-IV run against USGS 07207000; BoaterBeta publishes 200-1,000 cfs recommended references.
candidates.accessAndRisk: New Mexico Tourism describes continuous challenging whitewater, while the state park map marks campgrounds and fishing access rather than verified river-launch/take-out facilities for the whole run. No route-specific public water-entry pair and continuity review was found.
candidates.decision: Hold until boatable endpoint facilities, current river continuity and numeric-flow transfer across the reach are verified. The numeric range is rarely met at the Eagle Nest tailwater gauge and the route is a long Class III-IV commitment.

candidates.corridor: Canadian River, Rio Mora and other northeastern spring runs
candidates.routeEvidence: New Mexico Tourism documents 30-75 mile spring/wet-year runs on the Mora and Canadian rivers.
candidates.accessAndRisk: Seasonal flow may not occur in ordinary years; reviewed sources did not provide matched recreational scoring bands and a verified public on-water access chain suitable for a smaller day trip.
candidates.decision: Retain as research leads, not catalog routes, until current public endpoint, safety and same-reach flow evidence is available.

nextResearchTrigger: Revisit after Gila access status is confirmed by the Forest Service/local operator, Pecos access and strainer status are independently reviewed by experienced local paddlers, or an agency publishes boating access/flow guidance for Cimarron and other spring runs.
